text: The application for type approval of a retro-reflective device shall be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark or by his duly accredited representative.

Where the applicant chooses that the retro-reflector may be installed on a vehicle with different inclinations of the reference axis in respect to the vehicle reference planes and to the ground or, in the case of Classes IA, IB and IVA, rotate around its reference axis, the application shall specify this and these different conditions of installation shall be indicated in the communication form.
condition: at the choice of the applicant

text: The application for a retro-reflector shall be accompanied by drawings, in triplicate, in sufficient detail to permit identification of the type, showing geometrically the position(s) in which the retro-reflecting device may be fitted to the vehicle, and showing the position intended for the approval number and class indicator in relation to the circle of the approval mark.
For class IB or IIIB retro-reflectors, the drawings accompanying the application shall show details of installation.
The application for a retro-reflector shall be accompanied by a brief description giving the technical specifications of the materials of which the retro-reflecting optical unit is made.

The application for a retro-reflector shall be accompanied by samples of the retro-reflector of a colour specified by the manufacturer and, if necessary, the means of fixation, in the number specified in paragraphs 5.1. and 5.2.
The application for a retro-reflector shall be accompanied, if necessary, by two samples in other colour(s) for simultaneous or subsequent extension of the approval to devices in other colour(s).
condition: if extension to other colours is sought

text: The application for a retro-reflector of Class IVA shall be accompanied by samples of the retro-reflecting device and, if necessary, the means of fixation, in the number specified in paragraph 5.3.
The application for an advance warning triangle shall be accompanied by dimensional drawings in triplicate in sufficient detail to permit identification of the type.

The application for an advance warning triangle shall be accompanied by a brief description giving the technical specifications of the materials constituting the advance warning triangle and instructions for use.
The application for an advance warning triangle shall be accompanied by a copy of the instructions on its assembly for use.
The application for an advance warning triangle shall be accompanied by samples of the retro-reflective and of the fluorescent areas, in the number specified in paragraph 5.9.

The application for a retro-reflective marking plate shall be accompanied by drawings, in triplicate, sufficiently detailed to permit identification of the type, showing geometrically the position in which the marking plate is to be fitted to the rear end of the vehicle and the position intended for the approval number and the identification symbol in relation to the circle of the approval mark.
The application for a retro-reflective marking plate shall be accompanied by a brief description giving the technical specifications of the materials of which the retro-reflective areas are made.
The application for a retro-reflective marking plate shall be accompanied by a brief description giving the technical specifications of the materials of which the fluorescent areas are made.
The application for a retro-reflective marking plate shall be accompanied by samples of the retro-reflective and of the fluorescent areas, in the number specified in paragraphs 5.7. and 5.8.
The Type Approval Authority shall verify the existence of satisfactory arrangements for ensuring effective control of the conformity of production before type approval is granted.

The application for a retro-reflective marking material shall be accompanied by drawings, in triplicate, sufficiently detailed to permit identification of the type, showing geometrically the orientation in which the marking materials are to be fitted to a vehicle and the position intended for the approval number and the identification symbol in relation to the circle of the approval mark.
The application for a retro-reflective marking material shall be accompanied by a brief description giving the technical specifications of the retro-reflective marking materials.
The application for a retro-reflective marking material shall be accompanied by samples of the retro-reflective marking materials, as specified in paragraphs 5.4. and 5.5.

For a type of retro-reflective marking material differing only by the trade name or mark from an approved type, it shall be sufficient to submit a declaration by the manufacturer that the type submitted is identical (except in the trade name or mark) and has been produced by the same manufacturer as the type already approved, identified by its approval code, and two samples bearing the new trade name or mark or equivalent documentation.
condition: if the type differs only by the trade name or mark from an approved type

text: A separate approval is required for each retro-reflective device listed in paragraph 1.

Notice of approval or of extension or refusal or withdrawal of approval of a type of device shall be communicated to the Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement which apply this Regulation by means of a form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
An approval number shall be assigned to each type approved and shall be marked on the device following the requirements of paragraph 3.3.

The same Contracting Party shall not assign the same approval number to another type of device of the same function, except in the case of an extension of the approval to a device differing only in colour.

If the approval of a retro-reflecting device is extended to other such devices differing only in colour, the two samples in any other colour shall be required to meet only the colorimetric and photometric specifications, the other tests no longer being required; this does not apply to devices of Class IVA.
condition: extension of approval to devices differing only in colour; not for Class IVA

text: The symbol identifying a retro-reflector for motor vehicles (independent) shall be IA, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 5 mm.
The symbol identifying a retro-reflector for motor vehicles combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight shall be IB, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 5 mm.
The symbol identifying a retro-reflector for trailers (independent) shall be IIIA, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 5 mm.
The symbol identifying a retro-reflector for trailers combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight shall be IIIB, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 5 mm.
The symbol identifying a wide-angle retro-reflector shall be IVA, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 5 mm.
The symbol identifying retro-reflective marking material for contour/strip marking shall be C, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 8 mm.
The symbol identifying retro-reflective marking material for distinctive markings/graphics intended for a limited area shall be D, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 8 mm.
The symbol identifying retro-reflective marking material for distinctive markings/graphics intended for an extended area shall be E, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 8 mm.

The symbol identifying retro-reflective marking materials for distinctive markings or graphics as base or background in printing process for fully coloured logos and markings of class E in use which fulfil the requirements of class D materials shall be D/E, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 8 mm.
The symbol identifying retro-reflective marking material for extremities marking of class F shall be F, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 8 mm.

The symbol identifying retro-reflective marking plates for long or heavy vehicles comprising retro-reflective and fluorescent materials (class 1 or class 2) shall be RF, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 5 mm.
condition: class 1 or class 2 plates
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: The symbol identifying retro-reflective marking plates for long or heavy vehicles comprising retro-reflective only materials (class 3, class 4 or class 5) shall be RR, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 5 mm.
condition: class 3, 4 or 5 plates
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: The symbol identifying retro-reflective marking plates for slow moving vehicles comprising retro-reflective and fluorescent materials (class 1) shall be RF, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 5 mm.
condition: class 1 plates
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: The symbol identifying retro-reflective marking plates for slow moving vehicles comprising retro-reflective only materials (class 2) shall be RR, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 5 mm.
condition: class 2 plates
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: The symbol identifying an advance warning triangle of Type 1 shall be WT1, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 8 mm.
The symbol identifying an advance warning triangle of Type 2 shall be WT2, with minimum approval marking dimension a = 8 mm.
The change index for each retro-reflective device listed in Table 2 shall be 0 for the 00 series of amendments and 1 for the 01 series of amendments.

Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
All markings on the retro-reflective device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The size of the approval marking shall correspond to the value for "a" defined in Table 1.
The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number, placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
The approval marking may be replaced by the Unique Identifier, if available; the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I.
condition: if the Unique Identifier is available and used

text: Retro-reflective devices shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

Retro-reflectors of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
condition: if necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle(s) of rotation

text: Retro-reflective marking material of Class C, D, E or F shall bear an orientation mark "TOP" on any marking material whose retro-reflective system is not omni-rotational.
condition: if the retro-reflective system is not omni-rotational

text: Retro-reflective marking plates of Class 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 whose retro-reflective system is not omni-rotational shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the part of the plate which is intended to be the highest part of the plate when mounted on the vehicle.
condition: if the retro-reflective system is not omni-rotational

text: The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraph 3.3.4. shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
On retro-reflective marking material of Class C, D, E or F supplied as strips, the markings shall be positioned on the outside at least once in a 0.5 m distance.
condition: on strips

text: On retro-reflective marking material of Class C, D, E or F supplied as areas, the markings shall be positioned on the outside at least once within 100 mm x 100 mm.
condition: on areas

text: Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier may be affixed anywhere on them, provided that it is visible after their installation.
condition: if a single approval mark is used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps

text: The single approval mark on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be visible after their installation.
condition: if a single approval mark is used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps

text: No part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
condition: if a single approval mark is used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps

text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
condition: if a single approval mark is used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps

text: Every modification of the type of retro-reflective device shall be notified to the Type Approval Authority which approved the type, which may either consider the modifications unlikely to have an appreciable adverse effect or require a further report from the technical service.
condition: if the type is modified

text: Confirmation or refusal of approval, specifying the alterations, shall be communicated by the procedure specified in paragraph 3.2.2. to the Contracting Parties applying this Regulation.

The Type Approval Authority issuing the extension of approval shall assign a series number for such an extension and inform the other Contracting Parties by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
condition: if an extension of approval is issued

text: The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
Retro-reflectors approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
For retro-reflectors, the minimum requirements for conformity of production control procedures set forth in Annex 2 shall be complied with.
For retro-reflectors, the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector set forth in Annex 3 shall be complied with.

The authority which has granted type approval of retro-reflectors may at any time verify the conformity control methods applied in each production facility; the normal frequency of these verifications shall be once every two years.
Advance warning triangles approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved, with compliance with the requirements of paragraphs 4. and 5. verified.

The stability in time of the optical properties and colour of retro-reflecting optical units of advance warning triangles conforming to an approved type and in use shall be verified; in the event of a systematic deficiency (failure to meet paragraph 5), approval may be withdrawn.
Any retro-reflective marking material approved to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The conformity of production of retro-reflective marking material shall not be contested if the mean value of the photometric measurements of five specimens taken at random deviates unfavourably by not more than 20 per cent from the prescribed values given in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The conformity of production of retro-reflective marking material shall not be contested if the mean value of the colorimetric properties of five specimens taken at random meets the specifications of paragraphs 4. and 5., judged by visual inspection.

The authority which has granted type approval of retro-reflective marking material may at any time verify the conformity control methods applied in each production facility; the normal frequency of these verifications shall be once every two years.

Any retro-reflective marking plates approved to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5. (as to resistance to external agents, only paragraph 5.7.6.1. is applied).
For retro-reflective marking plates, the minimum requirements for conformity of production control procedures set forth in Annex 2 shall be complied with.
For retro-reflective marking plates, the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector set forth in Annex 3 shall be complied with.

The authority which has granted type approval of retro-reflective marking plates may at any time verify the conformity control methods applied in each production facility; the normal frequency of these verifications shall be once every two years.
The approval granted may be withdrawn if the requirements in this Regulation are not met.
condition: if the requirements are not met

text: A Contracting Party which withdraws an approval it has previously granted shall forthwith notify the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
condition: if an approval is withdrawn

text: If the holder of the approval completely ceases to manufacture an approved retro-reflective device, he shall so inform the authority which granted the approval.
condition: if production is definitively discontinued

text: Upon receiving the communication of definitive discontinuation of production, the authority which granted the approval shall inform the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
condition: if production is definitively discontinued

text: The Contracting Parties to the Agreement applying this Regulation shall communicate to the United Nations secretariat the names and addresses of the Technical Services responsible for conducting approval tests and of the Type Approval Authorities which grant approval and to which forms certifying approval or extension or refusal or withdrawal of approval, or the definitive discontinuation of production issued in other countries, are to be sent.

The requirements contained in sections 5. 'General specifications' and 6. 'Individual specifications' and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval shall apply to the retro-reflective device.

The requirements pertinent to each retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the retro-reflecting device is intended to be installed shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
condition: where verification at the moment of type approval is feasible

text: Retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
Retro-reflective devices must not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The means of attachment of the retro-reflective marking materials shall be durable and stable.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough and any protuberances they may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.
Where a retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, the unit and filter must be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
condition: if the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter

text: The colouring of retro-reflecting optical units and filters of retro-reflectors by means of paint or varnish is not permitted.
The night-time colour test specifications shall apply only to white, red or amber retro-reflective devices.
condition: white, red or amber retro-reflective devices

text: For testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, the device shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A, with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1. shall be used.

The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of the retro-reflective device shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.

White retro-reflective devices must not produce a selective reflection, that is to say, the trichromatic coordinates 'x' and 'y' of Standard Illuminant 'A' used to illuminate the retro-reflective device must not undergo a change of more than 0.01 after reflection by the retro-reflective device.
condition: white retro-reflective devices

text: For testing the daytime colour, the material shall be illuminated by the CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) using geometry (45a:0) or (0:45a) as described in Part 2 of Annex 4.
For the determination of the luminance factor, the sample shall be tested with the method as described in Part 2 of Annex 4.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.
The applicant shall submit ten samples of the retro-reflector for approval, which shall be tested in the chronological order as indicated in paragraph 5.1.7.

After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6.

At least one hour after the heat resistance test, the ten retro-reflector samples shall be examined as to their colorimetric characteristics in paragraph 5.1.5. and RI in paragraph 5.1.4., for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum values shall then be fully tested as shown in paragraph 5.1.4., and these two samples shall be kept by the laboratories for any further checks which may be found necessary.
The other eight retro-reflector samples shall be divided into four groups of two.

First group: the two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then, if this test is satisfactory, to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).

Second group: the two retro-reflector samples shall, if necessary, be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6, and then to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
Third group: the two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
Fourth group: the two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
condition: after the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1

text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have an RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4.
condition: after the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1

text: The RI verification after the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1. shall be performed only for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

When applying for approval, the applicant shall specify one or more or a range of axis of reference of the retro-reflector, corresponding to the illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the table of coefficients of luminous intensity RI.

In the case where more than one or a range of different axis of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the photometric measurements of the retro-reflector shall be repeated making reference each time to a different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range specified by the manufacturer.
condition: if more than one or a range of axes of reference are specified

text: For photometric measurements of Class IA or IB retro-reflectors, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system of the retro-reflective device as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered, and the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.
The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the area of the retro-reflector to be used for photometric measurements.

The RI values of retro-reflectors shall be measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4 and must be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

condition: white colour

condition: amber colour

text: The testing of the colour for the retro-reflector (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux of the retro-reflector must be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

text: All ten samples (a to j) of Class IA, IB, IIIA and IIIB retro-reflectors shall be subjected to visual inspection of general specifications and of shapes and dimensions (Annex 5).

Class IA, IB, IIIA and IIIB retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the water test (10 min. in normal position, 10 min. in inverted position, visual inspection), followed by colorimetry (paragraph 4.2.) and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

Class IA, IB, IIIA and IIIB retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the motor fuels test (Part 1 of Annex 7, 5 min., visual inspection) and the oils test (Part 2 of Annex 7, 5 min., visual inspection), followed by colorimetry (paragraph 4.2.) and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

Class IA, IB, IIIA and IIIB retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the corrosion test (Part 4 of Annex 6: 24 hours, 2 hours interval, 24 hours, visual inspection) and the rear face test (1 min., visual inspection), followed by colorimetry (paragraph 4.2.) and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

All ten samples (a to j) of Class IVA retro-reflectors shall be subjected to visual inspection of general specifications and of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), then to the heat test of Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 h at 65 °C ± 2°C) with visual inspection for distortion, followed by colorimetry (paragraph 4.2.) and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
Two samples of Class IVA retro-reflectors shall be subjected to complete photometry according to Part 1 of Annex 4.
Class IVA retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the water test of Part 2 of Annex 6 (10 min. in normal position, 10 min. in inverted position, visual inspection).

Class IVA retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the motor fuels test (Part 1 of Annex 7, 5 min., visual inspection) and the oils test (Part 2 of Annex 7, 5 min., visual inspection), followed by colorimetry (paragraph 4.2.) and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

Class IVA retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the corrosion test (Part 4 of Annex 6: 24 hours, 2 hours' interval, 24 hours, visual inspection) and the rear face test (1 min., visual inspection).

Class IVA retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the impact test (Part 4 of Annex 8, visual inspection), followed by colorimetry (paragraph 4.2.) and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

For advance warning triangles of type 2, the luminance factor of the fluorescent materials, including the luminance by reflection and fluorescence, shall be βv,R ≥ 0.25.

For advance warning triangles, the largest measured trichromatic coordinate y value according to paragraph 4.2.1. (night-time colour) shall be smaller or equal to the largest measured trichromatic coordinate y value according to paragraph 4.2.2. (daytime colour).
