text: The conformity of production requirements for retro-reflective devices shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.

With respect to photometric performances, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if, when testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be complied with.

For each type of retro-reflective device the holder of the approval mark shall carry out at least the tests listed in Annex 2, at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation.

If any sampling shows non-conformity with regard to the type of test concerned, further samples shall be taken and tested, and the manufacturer shall take steps to ensure the conformity of the production concerned.
condition: if any sampling shows non-conformity

text: The manufacturer's conformity tests shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the resistance to penetration of water of the retro-reflective devices.
Conformity tests shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.

In any test of conformity carried out by the manufacturer, equivalent methods may be used only with the consent of the Type Approval Authority, and the manufacturer is responsible for proving that the applied methods are equivalent to those laid down in this Regulation.
condition: if equivalent test methods are used

text: Conformity testing shall be based on regular calibration of test apparatus and its correlation with measurements made by a Type Approval Authority.
In all cases the reference methods shall be those of this Regulation, particularly for the purpose of administrative verification and sampling.

Samples of retro-reflective devices shall be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch (a set of retro-reflective devices of the same type, defined according to the production methods of the manufacturer).

The conformity assessment shall in general cover series production from individual factories; a manufacturer may group together records concerning the same type from several factories only provided these operate under the same quality system and quality management.
condition: if records from several factories are grouped

text: The sampled retro-reflective device shall be subjected to photometric measurements at the points and the chromaticity coordinates provided for in the Regulation.

The manufacturer shall carry out a statistical study of the test results and define, in agreement with the Type Approval Authority, criteria governing the acceptability of his products in order to meet the specifications for verification of conformity of products in paragraph 3.5.1.

The criteria governing acceptability shall be such that, with a confidence level of 95 per cent, the minimum probability of passing a spot check in accordance with Annex 3 (first sampling) would be 0.95.

In sampling by an inspector, the conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

With respect to photometric performance in sampling by an inspector, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if no measured value of any retro-reflective device chosen at random deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
In photometric conformity testing by an inspector, retro-reflective devices with apparent defects are disregarded.
In sampling by an inspector, the chromaticity coordinates of the retro-reflective devices shall be complied with.
In the first sampling four retro-reflective devices shall be selected at random; the first sample of two is marked A, the second sample of two is marked B.

The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples A and B (all four retro-reflective devices) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both devices of sample A is not more than 0 per cent, the measurement can be closed.
condition: first sampling

text: The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of samples A or B is more than 20 per cent; the manufacturer shall be requested to bring his production in line with the requirements (alignment) and a repeated sampling according to paragraph 3 shall be carried out within two months' time after the notification.
condition: if at least one specimen of samples A or B deviates by more than 20 per cent

text: The samples A and B shall be retained by the Technical Service until the entire CoP process is finished.
condition: if conformity is contested after the first sampling

text: In the first repeated sampling a sample of four retro-reflective devices shall be selected at random from stock manufactured after alignment; the first sample of two is marked C, the second sample of two is marked D.
condition: after alignment following the first sampling

text: The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples C and D (all four retro-reflective devices) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both devices of sample C is not more than 0 per cent, the measurement can be closed.
condition: first repeated sampling

text: The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of samples C or D is more than 20 per cent but the deviation of all specimens is not more than 30 per cent; the manufacturer shall be requested again to align his production and a second repeated sampling according to paragraph 4 shall be carried out within two months' time after the notification.
condition: if one specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 20 per cent but none by more than 30 per cent

text: The samples C and D shall be retained by the Technical Service until the entire CoP process is finished.
condition: if conformity is contested after the first repeated sampling

text: If the deviation of one specimen of samples C and D is more than 30 per cent, the approval shall be withdrawn and paragraph 5 of Annex 3 shall be applied.
condition: if one specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 30 per cent

text: In the second repeated sampling a sample of four retro-reflective devices shall be selected at random from stock manufactured after alignment; the first sample of two is marked E, the second sample of two is marked F.
condition: after second alignment

text: The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples E and F (all four retro-reflective devices) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both devices of sample E is not more than 0 per cent, the measurement can be closed.
condition: second repeated sampling

text: The conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F is more than 20 per cent; in this case the approval shall be withdrawn and paragraph 5 of Annex 3 shall be applied.
condition: if at least one specimen of samples E or F deviates by more than 20 per cent

text: Approval shall be withdrawn according to paragraph 3.6. of this Regulation.
condition: if withdrawal is required by Annex 3 sampling results

text: One of the retro-reflectors of sample A after the first sampling shall be tested for resistance to water penetration according to paragraph 1 of Part 2 of Annex 6, and is acceptable if the test is passed; if it fails, the two retro-reflective devices of sample B shall be subjected to the same procedure and both shall pass the test.

In the case of the advance warning triangle, sample A shall be tested for resistance to water penetration according to paragraph 2 of Part 2 of Annex 6; if the test on sample A is not complied with, the two devices of sample B shall be subjected to the same procedure and both shall pass the test.

Specimens of one of the rear marking plates of sample A after the first sampling shall be tested according to the procedures described in Annexes 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 16 and 18; the plate is acceptable if the tests are passed, otherwise the two rear marking plates of sample B shall be subjected to the same procedure and both shall pass the test.

When the RI of a retro-reflective device is measured for β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained whether any mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the device; if there is any such effect, a reading shall be taken with β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
condition: if a mirror effect is produced

text: With an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5) and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices not marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes of reference to the position of minimum RI, which must conform to the value specified in paragraph 5.
condition: device not marked TOP

text: When the RI of a retro-reflective device not marked "TOP" is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the device shall be placed in the position corresponding to the minimum-RI value of ε; if the specified values are not attained, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference ±5° from that position.
condition: device not marked TOP

text: With an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 4) and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes ±5°, and the RI must not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during this rotation.
condition: device marked TOP

text: If for the direction β1 = β2 = 0° and for ε = 0° the RI exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.
condition: if RI at β1 = β2 = 0°, ε = 0° exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more

text: The CIE-angular system as shown in Figure A4-I shall be used for specifying and measuring retro-reflective devices and marking materials.
The goniometer used for measuring retro-reflective devices and marking materials shall embody the CIE angular system as shown in Figure A4-II or an equivalent arrangement of components.

For testing the retro-reflection, the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
In the measuring geometry for retro-reflective devices the angular diameter of the source shall be δ ≤ 10'.
In the measuring geometry for retro-reflective devices the angular diameter of the measuring device shall be γ ≤ 10'.
In the measuring geometry for retro-reflective devices the angular diameter of the illuminated area shall be η ≤ 80'.
During photometric measurements of retro-reflective devices, stray reflections should be avoided by appropriate masking.
The measuring distance shall be chosen such that at least the limits for the angles δ, γ and η are respected, but not lower than 10 m.

The illuminance over the useful area of the retro-reflective device, measured perpendicular to the incident light, shall be sufficiently uniform, checked with a measuring element whose sensitive area is not greater than one-tenth of the area examined, with the variation of illuminance complying with max/min ≤ 1.05.
The photometer head shall be corrected to the spectral luminous efficiency for the CIE standard photometric observer in photopic vision.

The photometer head shall not show a perceptible change in local sensitivity within the area of its aperture; otherwise suitable provisions shall be added, e.g. a diffusing window at a certain distance in front of the sensitive surface.

In retro-reflection photometry, the background to the sample and the framework of the sample holder should be matt black, and the field of view of the photometer head and the spread of light from both the sample and the source shall be restricted as much as possible.
Reflections from the floor and walls over the test distances shall be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles.

Residual stray light shall be measured with the sample covered by an opaque matt black surface, zigzag folded black paper of the same size and shape, or a suitably oriented specular black surface with a light trap, and this value shall be subtracted from that measured on the retro-reflective device.

The light source and photometer head should remain stable throughout the test, the laboratory ambient temperature should not vary significantly during this period, and sufficient time should be allowed for the apparatus to stabilize before commencing measurements.

For testing the daytime colour and luminance factor of retro-reflective material, illumination by CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) using geometry (45a:0) shall be used.

Measurements of daytime colour shall be done with a spectrophotometer in accordance with Publication CIE 15:2004, either illuminated poly-chromatically or with a monochromator providing stepwise the CIE Standard Illuminant D65 at an angle 45° to the normal and viewed along the normal (geometry 45/0).
When a monochromator is used for daytime colour measurement, the stepwise resolution Δλ shall be not larger than 10 nm.
condition: if a monochromator providing stepwise illumination is used

text: Similar simulation spectra are allowed for daytime colour measurement only if verified that the colorimetric measuring procedure is of the same accuracy, the quality of the D65 simulation being assessed by the method described in ISO 23603:2005(E)/CIE S 012/E:2004.
condition: if simulation spectra are used

text: The spectral distribution of the illuminant for daytime colour measurement shall be in category BC (CIELAB) or better.
The measurement area for daytime colour measurement shall be at least minimum 4.0 cm².

The apertures of the light source and the receiver of the daytime colour measuring apparatus shall have sufficient dimensions in proportion to distances to ensure compliance with the CIE 15 recommendations for the annular 45°a:0° geometry (illumination between cones of 40° and 50° half angle; collection within a 5° half-angle cone).

The luminance factor βv,R of the sample shall be determined by relating the luminance L of the sample to the luminance L0 of a perfect diffuser of known luminance factor under identical conditions of illumination and observation, or, where the colour of the fluorescent material has been colorimetrically determined in compliance with paragraph 1, by the ratio of the tristimulus value Y of the sample to the tristimulus value Y0 of the perfect diffuser.
The approval granting authority has the right to test the optical properties stability of a retro-reflecting material in use (when used for marking or as distinctive markings/graphics).
condition: when used for marking or as distinctive markings/graphics

text: If "systematic failures in use" occur for a type of retro-reflective material, the tested material samples shall be transferred for appraisal to the authority which granted approval.
condition: if systematic failures in use occur

text: If other criteria are missing, "systematic failures in use" for a type of retro-reflective material is to be established according to paragraph 5 in Part 3 of Annex 4.
condition: if other criteria are missing

text: The authority which granted approval shall have the right to check the stability in time of the optical properties of a type of rear marking plate in service.

If a type of rear marking plate in use exhibits a systematic defect, the Type Approval Authorities of other countries carrying out checks shall transmit to the authority which granted approval, with a request for its opinion, any components removed for examination.
condition: if a systematic defect is exhibited in use

text: In the absence of other criteria, the concept of "systematic defect" of a type of rear marking plate in use shall be interpreted in conformity with the intention of paragraph 5 of Part 3 of Annex 4.
condition: in the absence of other criteria

text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of retro-reflectors of Class IA or IB shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for Class IIIA and IIIB retro-reflectors from an observation distance of 10 metres.
The illuminating surfaces of retro-reflectors of Classes IIIA and IIIB must have the shape of an equilateral triangle.
If the word "TOP" is inscribed in one corner of a Class IIIA or IIIB retro-reflector, the apex of that corner must be directed upwards.
condition: if the word TOP is inscribed in one corner

text: The illuminating surface of a Class IIIA or IIIB retro-reflector may have at its centre a triangular, non-retro-reflecting area only with sides parallel to those of the outer triangle.
condition: if a central non-retro-reflecting area is provided

text: Whether or not the illuminating surface of a Class IIIA or IIIB retro-reflector is continuous, the shortest distance between two adjacent retro-reflecting optical units must not exceed 15 mm.

The illuminating surface of a Class IIIA or IIIB retro-reflector shall be considered continuous only if the edges of the illuminating surfaces of adjacent separate optical units are parallel and the optical units are evenly distributed over the whole solid surface of the triangle.

If the illuminated surface of a Class IIIA or IIIB retro-reflector is not continuous, the number of separate retro-reflecting optical units including the corner units shall not be less than four on each side of the triangle.
condition: if the illuminated surface is not continuous

text: The separate retro-reflecting optical units of a Class IIIA or IIIB retro-reflector shall not be replaceable unless they consist of approved retro-reflective devices of Class IA.
condition: if the illuminated surface is not continuous

text: The outside edges of the illuminating surfaces of triangular retro-reflectors of Classes IIIA and IIIB shall be between 150 and 200 mm long.

In the case of Class IIIA or IIIB retro-reflectors of hollow-triangle type, the width of the sides, measured at right angles to the latter, shall be equal to at least 20 per cent of the effective length between the extremities of the illuminating surface.
condition: for devices of hollow-triangle type

text: The shape of the light emitting surfaces of Class IVA retro-reflectors shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for Class IIIA and IIIB retro-reflectors from an observation distance of 10 metres.
The light emitting surface of a Class IVA retro-reflector must be at least 25 cm2.
Compliance of retro-reflectors with the shape and dimension specifications of Annex 5 paragraphs 1 to 3 shall be verified by visual inspection.
Class C retro-reflective markings shall be made of strips of retro-reflective material.
The width of a Class C retro-reflective marking material shall be 50 mm +10/-0 mm.
The minimum length of an element of a Class C retro-reflective marking material shall be such that at least one approval mark is visible.
Class F and Class 5 markings shall be made of strips of retro-reflective material or plates.
condition: for Class F materials and Class 5 plates
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: Class F and Class 5 retro-reflective markings shall consist of red and white diagonal stripes downwards at 45° ± 1° as shown in Figures A5-II, A5-III and A5-IV.
condition: for Class F materials and Class 5 plates
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: The basic standard area of Class F and Class 5 retro-reflective markings is a square of 141 mm ± 1 mm in length subdivided diagonally into a white half and a red half.
condition: for Class F materials and Class 5 plates
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: The minimum length of an element of a Class F retro-reflective marking material or Class 5 plate shall incorporate a minimum of 9 standard areas on large vehicles with available mounting space, but may be reduced to a minimum of 3 standard areas on vehicles with limited mounting space.
condition: 9 standard areas on large vehicles with available mounting space; 3 on vehicles with limited mounting space
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: HLV rear marking plates of Class 1, 2, 3 or 4 shall be rectangular in shape for mounting at the rear of vehicles.
condition: for Classes 1, 2, 3 or 4
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: HLV rear marking plates for mounting on trailers and semi-trailers shall have a yellow retro-reflective background with a red fluorescent or retro-reflective border.
condition: for plates intended for trailers and semi-trailers
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: HLV rear marking plates for mounting on non-articulated vehicles (tractors or trucks) shall be of the chevron type with alternate, oblique stripes of yellow retro-reflective and red fluorescent or retro-reflective materials or devices.
condition: for plates intended for non-articulated vehicles (tractors or trucks)
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: The minimum total summarized length of a set of HLV rear marking plates consisting only of one, two or four marking plates with retro-reflective and fluorescent materials shall be 1,130 mm, and the maximum total length shall be 2,300 mm.
condition: for sets of one, two or four plates with retro-reflective and fluorescent materials
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: The width of an HLV rear marking plate for trucks and tractors shall be 140 ± 10 mm.
condition: for trucks and tractors
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: The width of an HLV rear marking plate for trailers and semi-trailers shall be 200 +30/-5 mm.
condition: for trailers and semi-trailers
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: The length of each HLV rear marking plate in a set of two plates for trucks and tractors may be reduced to a minimum of 130 mm only provided that the width is increased such that the area of each marking is at least 735 cm2, does not exceed 1,725 cm2 and the marking plates are rectangular.
condition: for a set of two plates for trucks and tractors with reduced length
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: The width of the red fluorescent border of HLV rear marking plates for trailers and semi-trailers shall be 40 mm ± 1 mm.
condition: for trailers and semi-trailers
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: The slope of the oblique stripes of the chevron band of HLV rear marking plates shall be 45° ± 5°.
condition: for chevron-type plates
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: The width of the stripes of the chevron band of HLV rear marking plates shall be 100 mm ± 2.5 mm.
condition: for chevron-type plates
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: HLV rear marking plates supplied in sets shall form matching pairs.
condition: if supplied in sets
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: SMV rear marking plates shall be in the shape of an equilateral triangle with truncated corners, for mounting with one apex upwards at the rear of slow-moving vehicles.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: SMV rear marking plates of class 1 shall have a red fluorescent centre and red retro-reflective borders made of either retro-reflective material or coating or of plastic corner-cube reflectors.
condition: for class 1
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: SMV rear marking plates of class 2 shall have a retro-reflective centre.
condition: for class 2
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: The length of the base of the enclosed fluorescent triangle (class 1) or retro-reflective triangle (class 2) of SMV rear marking plates shall be minimum 350 mm and maximum 365 mm.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: The width of the light-emitting surface of the red retro-reflective border of SMV rear marking plates shall be minimum 45 mm and maximum 48 mm.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: The theoretical sides of the advance warning triangle shall be 500 ± 50 mm long.
In an advance warning triangle of type 1, the retro-reflecting units shall be arranged along the edge within a strip of an unvarying width between 25 mm and 50 mm.
In an advance warning triangle of type 2 with fluorescent retro-reflecting material, the unvarying width of the retro-reflecting strip shall be between 50 mm and 85 mm.
condition: with fluorescent retro-reflecting material

text: Any edging between the outer edge of the advance warning triangle and the retro-reflecting strip shall be not more than 5 mm wide (not necessarily red-coloured).
condition: if an edging is provided

text: If the retro-reflecting strip of the advance warning triangle is not continuous, the free area of the supporting material shall be red.
condition: if the retro-reflecting strip is not continuous

text: In an advance warning triangle of type 1, the fluorescent surface shall be continuous to the retro-reflecting units.
In an advance warning triangle of type 1, the fluorescent surface shall be arranged symmetrically along the three sides of the triangle.
In an advance warning triangle of type 1, when in use, the fluorescent surface area shall be not less than 315 cm2.
condition: when in use

text: In an advance warning triangle of type 1, any edging, continuous or not, placed between the retro-reflecting surface and the fluorescent surface shall be not more than 5 mm wide (not necessarily red-coloured).
condition: if an edging is provided

text: The side of the open centre of the advance warning triangle shall have a minimum length of 70 mm.
The distance between the supporting surface and the lower side of the advance warning triangle shall not exceed 300 mm.
The fluorescent retro-reflecting material of the advance warning triangle shall be coloured in the mass, either in the retro-reflective elements or as solid surface layer.

In the heat resistance test for moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle type 1, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
condition: for moulded plastics reflectors
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: In the heat resistance test for flexible materials of Classes C, D, E, F, marking plates of Classes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and advance warning triangle type 2, a section of a sample unit not less than 300 mm long shall be kept for 12 hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C, then kept for 12 hours at -20 °C ± 2 °C, and examined after a recovery time of 4 hours under normal laboratory conditions.
condition: for flexible materials
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component must be visible.

For the water penetration test, retro-reflectors (whether part of a lamp or not) or a sample unit of retro-reflective marking shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface; the test shall be repeated after turning the device through 180° so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water; the sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.

In the water penetration test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit; if visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device shall not be considered to have passed the test.

For retro-reflectors, if visual inspection after the water penetration test does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, the RI shall be measured by the method of paragraph 5.1.3.2.2., the device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
condition: if visual inspection does not reveal water or in case of doubt

text: For a sample unit of retro-reflective marking, if visual inspection after the water penetration test does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, the coefficient of retro-reflection R' shall be measured, the sample unit being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
condition: if visual inspection does not reveal water or in case of doubt

text: For the water resistance test of the advance warning triangle (collapsible triangles assembled as for use), the triangle shall be immersed for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface about 20 mm below the water surface, and immediately afterwards immersed under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.

After the water resistance test, no water shall have penetrated to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflective device of the advance warning triangle; if visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device has not passed the test. Water or water vapour penetration into the edges of fluorescent retro-reflecting materials shall not be deemed to indicate failure.

If visual inspection after the water resistance test of the advance warning triangle does not reveal water, or in case of doubt, the RI shall again be measured under the same conditions after the device has been gently shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
condition: if visual inspection does not reveal water or in case of doubt

text: After the water resistance test, the RI of the advance warning triangle shall not have diminished by more than 40 per cent of the values recorded before the test.
condition: if visual inspection does not reveal water or in case of doubt

text: In the water test, the advance warning triangle (collapsible triangles assembled as for use) shall be immersed flat for two hours on the bottom of a tank containing water at 25 °C ± 5 °C, with the active face upwards and 5 cm under the water surface, then removed and dried.
After the water test, no part of the advance warning triangle may exhibit clear signs of deterioration which might impair the effectiveness of the triangle.

For the water resistance test of retro-reflective marking plates, a section of a sample unit not less than 300 mm long shall be immersed in distilled water at a temperature of 23 ± 5ºC for a period of 18 hours and then left to dry for 24 hours under normal laboratory conditions, after which the section shall be examined.

After the water resistance test, no part of the retro-reflective marking plate section inside 10 mm from the cut edge shall show evidence of deterioration which would reduce the effectiveness of the plate.
As an alternative water penetration test for retro-reflectors of Classes IB and IIIB, at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture and dust tests of Part 3 of Annex 6 shall be applied.
condition: at the request of the manufacturer

text: The water spray cabinet for the moisture test shall be equipped with a nozzle(s) providing a solid cone water spray of sufficient angle to completely cover the sample device, with the nozzle centreline directed downward at an angle of 45° ± 5° to the vertical axis of a rotating test platform.
condition: if the alternative moisture test is applied

text: The rotating test platform of the moisture test shall have a minimum diameter of 140 mm and rotate about a vertical axis in the centre of the cabinet.
condition: if the alternative moisture test is applied

text: The precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min, measured with a vertical cylindrical collector centred on the vertical axis of the rotating test platform, of height 100 mm and inside diameter a minimum of 140 mm.
condition: if the alternative moisture test is applied

text: For the water spray test, the sample device shall be mounted on a test fixture with initial RI measured and recorded before being subjected to the water spray.
condition: if the alternative moisture test is applied

text: During the water spray test all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
condition: if the alternative moisture test is applied

text: During the water spray test the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.
condition: if the alternative moisture test is applied

text: If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated during the water spray test at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
condition: if the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions

text: The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
condition: if the alternative moisture test is applied

text: After the water spray test, the rotation and water spray shall be turned OFF and the device allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed.
condition: if the alternative moisture test is applied

text: Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation and no standing pool of water shall be formed, or be capable of being formed by tapping or tilting the device.
condition: if the alternative moisture test is applied

text: After the drain period, the RI of the device shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after having dried the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth.
condition: if the alternative moisture test is applied

text: The interior of the dust exposure test chamber shall be cubical in shape, 0.9 to 1.5 m per side (bottom may be hopper shaped), with an internal volume, not including a hopper shaped bottom, of 2 m3 maximum, charged with 3 to 5 kg of the test dust, and capable of agitating the dust by compressed air or blower fans so that it is diffused throughout the chamber.
condition: if the alternative dust test is applied

text: The test dust used in the dust exposure test shall be fine powdered cement in accordance with standard ASTM C 150-84.
condition: if the alternative dust test is applied

text: For the dust exposure test, the sample device shall be mounted on a test fixture with the initial RI measured and recorded before exposure to dust.
condition: if the alternative dust test is applied

text: During the dust exposure test all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
condition: if the alternative dust test is applied

text: The mounted device shall be placed in the dust chamber no closer than 150 mm from a wall, and devices with a length exceeding 600 mm shall be horizontally centred in the test chamber.
condition: if the alternative dust test is applied

text: The test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible by compressed air or blower(s) at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours, and allowed to settle between the agitation periods.
condition: if the alternative dust test is applied

text: Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2.
condition: if the alternative dust test is applied

text: Retro-reflective devices must be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.

The resistance of the front surface of the retro-reflective device to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration shall be checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked, the testing being as described in ISO Standard 9227:2017.

For the corrosion test, the retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to a saline mist for 50 hours, comprising two exposure periods of 24 hours each separated by a two-hour interval during which the sample is allowed to dry.

For retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
condition: if the device has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion

text: Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

After the corrosion test and a recovery period of 48 hours, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, measured at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
Before measuring the coefficient of retro-reflection after the corrosion test, the surface shall be cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist.

For the rear face resistance test of mirror-backed moulded plastics reflectors (Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangle type 1), the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.
condition: in the case of moulded plastics reflectors with accessible mirror-backed rear face

text: After brushing, for moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the rear face for one minute, then removed and the device left to dry.
condition: in the case of moulded plastics reflectors with accessible mirror-backed rear face

text: After brushing, for moulded plastics reflectors of advance warning triangles of type 1, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be covered or thoroughly wetted for one minute with the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7, after which the fuel shall be removed and the device allowed to dry.
condition: in the case of moulded plastics reflectors with accessible mirror-backed rear face

text: As soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side of the mirror-backed retro-reflective device shall be brushed with the same brush as before.
The RI of the mirror-backed retro-reflective device shall then be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.

For the retro-reflector of an advance warning triangle of type 1, the RI after the rear face resistance test shall not have diminished by more than 40 per cent of the values recorded before the test; this test is not applicable to fluorescent retro-reflecting material.
condition: not applicable for fluorescent retro-reflecting material

text: The accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be in accordance with EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013, shall be capable to control temperature and relative humidity and shall be equipped with a water spray system.
The water spray system of the weathering apparatus shall be capable to spray a minimum of 0.3 ml/cm² within 5 minutes.
The spray water used in the weathering test shall be in accordance with the requirements of EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
For temperature measurement in the weathering test, either a Black-Standard thermometer (TM1) or a Black-Panel thermometer (TM2) may be used.
The weathering test method used (TM1 or TM2) shall be specified in the report.
Retro-reflective devices shall be exposed in the weathering test in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1 for a period of 500 hours.
Fluorescent materials shall be exposed in the weathering test in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1 for a period of 100 hours.

With method TM1 (Black-standard thermometer), the weathering test shall use cycle No. 1 of EN ISO 4892-2:2013: 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, broadband (300 to 400 nm) irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m², narrowband (340 nm) irradiance 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m², black-standard temperature 65 ± 3 °C and relative humidity 50 ± 10 %.
condition: if method TM1 is used

text: With method TM2 (Black-panel thermometer), the weathering test shall use cycle No. 4 of EN ISO 4892-2:2013: 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, broadband (300 to 400 nm) irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m², narrowband (340 nm) irradiance 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m², black-panel temperature 63 ± 3 °C and relative humidity 50 ± 10 %.
condition: if method TM2 is used

text: Preparation of weathering test specimens shall be in accordance with the general guidelines given in EN ISO 4892-2:2013.

For the fuel resistance test of a retro-reflective device, the outer surface and in particular the illuminating surface shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol, and the surface inspected visually after about five minutes.
After the fuel resistance test, the surface of the retro-reflective device must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.

For the fuel resistance test of retro-reflective marking material, a section of a sample unit not less than 300 mm long shall be immersed for one minute in the test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol and after removal wiped dry with a soft cloth.
After the fuel resistance test, the surface of the retro-reflective marking material shall not show any visible change which would reduce its effective performance.

For the fuel resistance test of advance warning triangles, the triangle and its protective cover shall be immersed separately for 60 seconds in a mixture of 70 per cent n-heptane and 30 per cent toluene, removed and drained of excess liquid, then the triangle placed in its cover and the unit laid flat in a still atmosphere.
When completely dried after the fuel test, the advance warning triangle shall not adhere to its protective cover.
condition: if supplied with a protective cover

text: When completely dried after the fuel test, there shall be no visually noticeable change on the surface of the advance warning triangle and it shall not present apparent detrimental modifications; however, slight surface cracks may be tolerated.

For the lubricating oil resistance test of moulded plastics reflectors (Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangle type 1), the outer surface and in particular the illuminating surface shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil, cleaned after about 5 minutes, and the RI then measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2.
condition: in the case of moulded plastics reflectors

text: A test sample of retro-reflective marking material smeared with a mixture of detergent lubricating oil and graphite shall be easily cleaned without damage to the retro-reflective surface when wiped with a mild aliphatic solvent such as n-heptane, followed by washing with a neutral detergent.

When subjected to continuous power washing for 60 seconds in its normal mounting conditions, a test sample of retro-reflective marking material shall show no damage to the retro-reflective surface, no delamination from the substrate and no separation from the sample mounting surface.

The power washing test shall use a water/wash solution pressure of 8 ± 0.2 MPa, temperature of 60 +0/-5 °C, flow rate of 7 ± 1 l/min, the cleaning wand tip at 600 ± 20 mm from the retro-reflective surface, held at no greater angle than 45 degrees from perpendicular to the surface, with a 40-degree nozzle creating a wide fan pattern.
For the bonding strength test of retro-reflective marking material, an aluminium plate shall be used as substrate and the application shall be done according to the manufacturer's recommendation.
condition: in the case of adhesive materials

text: The adhesion of retro-reflective material shall be determined after 24 hours curing time by utilising a 90-degree peel on a tensile strength testing machine.
condition: in the case of adhesive materials

text: The adhesive retro-reflective material shall not be easily removable without damaging the material.
condition: in the case of adhesive materials

text: The adhesive retro-reflective material shall need a force of at least 10 N per 25 mm width at a constant speed of 300 mm per minute to be removed from its substrate.
condition: in the case of adhesive materials

text: For retro-reflective marking material to be adhered to a flexible substrate (i.e. tarpaulin), a specimen of the sample unit measuring 50 mm by 300 mm shall be bent once lengthwise around a 3.2 mm mandrel with adhesive contacting the mandrel for a period of 1 second.
condition: for samples to be adhered to a flexible substrate

text: The flexing test temperature shall be 23 °C ± 2 °C.
condition: for samples to be adhered to a flexible substrate

text: After the flexing test, the specimen of retro-reflective marking material shall not have cracking of the surface and shall not show any visible change that would reduce its effective performance.
condition: for samples to be adhered to a flexible substrate

text: When a 25 mm diameter solid steel ball is dropped from a height of 2 m onto the retro-reflective and fluorescent surfaces of a supported rear marking plate at an ambient temperature of 23 ± 2 ºC, the material shall show no cracking or separation from the substrate at a distance of more than 5 mm from the impacted area.
condition: except for plastics corner-cube reflectors

text: For the impact test of Class IVA retro-reflectors, the device shall be mounted similarly to its mounting on the vehicle but with the lens faced horizontal and directed upwards, and a 13 mm diameter polished solid steel ball shall be dropped once vertically onto the central part of the lens from a height of 0.76 m, guided but not restricted in free fall.
When tested at room temperature with the ball impact method, the lens of the Class IVA retro-reflector shall not crack.

For the rigidity test of HLV rear marking plates of Classes 1 to 5, the plate shall be placed on two supports parallel to its shorter edge with the distance from either support to the adjacent edge not exceeding L/10 (L being the greater overall dimension), loaded with bags of shot or dry sand to a uniformly distributed pressure of 1.5 kN/m2, and the deflection measured midway between the supports.
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: In the rigidity test, the maximum deflection of the HLV rear marking plate under the test load shall not exceed one twentieth of the distance between the supports.
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: In the rigidity test, the residual deflection of the HLV rear marking plate after removal of the load shall not exceed one fifth of the measured deflection under load.
applies_to: rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles

text: For the rigidity test of SMV rear marking plates of Classes 1 and 2, the triangular plate shall be strongly held on one of its long sides with the clamps not encroaching over more than 20 mm, and a force of 10 N perpendicular to the plane shall be applied to the opposite apex.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: Under the 10 N rigidity test force, the apex of the SMV rear marking plate shall not move in the direction of the force by more than 40 mm.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: After removal of the force, the SMV rear marking plate shall visibly return to its initial position and the residual deflection shall not be more than 5 mm.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: The advance warning triangle shall be required to pass the test of clearance to ground described in Annex 9 paragraph 1.

For the clearance to ground test of the advance warning triangle, the test apparatus shown in Figure A5-X, which has the form of an inverted hollow pyramid, shall be placed on a horizontal base plane.

For the clearance to ground test, the individual supports to the ground of the advance warning triangle shall be placed one after another in the square hole σ of the test apparatus, and during the test of each support a position of the test apparatus favourable for the triangle shall be found which ensures the conditions of paragraphs 1.1.2.1 and 1.1.2.2.
During the clearance to ground test of each support, all supports of the advance warning triangle shall rest simultaneously on the base plane.

During the clearance to ground test, outside the area covered by the test apparatus, the distance between the base plane and parts of the advance warning triangle as well as of the supporting device shall be at least 50 mm (with the exception of the supports proper).

For the mechanical solidity test, when the advance warning triangle has been set up as required by the manufacturer and its bases are firmly held, a force of 2 N shall be applied to the apex of the triangle parallel to the supporting surface and normal to the lower side of the triangle.
In the mechanical solidity test, the apex of the advance warning triangle shall not move more than 5 cm in the direction in which the force is exerted.
After the mechanical solidity test, the position of the advance warning triangle shall not be significantly different from its original position.
For the heat resistance test, the advance warning triangle, in its protective cover if provided, shall be kept for 12 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 60 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat resistance test, no cracking or noticeable distortion of the advance warning triangle shall be visible, in particular of the retro-reflective device.
After the heat resistance test, the protective cover of the advance warning triangle shall be readily openable and shall not adhere to the triangle.
condition: if a protective cover is provided

text: After the heat-resistance test and subsequent storage for 12 consecutive hours at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C, the advance warning triangle, in its protective cover, is to be kept for another 12 hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of -40 °C ± 2 °C.
Immediately after removal from the cold room, no fractures or any visible distortion shall be noticeable on the advance warning triangle and especially on its optical parts.
Immediately after removal from the cold room, the protective cover of the advance warning triangle shall be properly openable, and it shall neither tear nor adhere to the advance warning triangle.
condition: if a protective cover is provided

text: The sandy beach test shall be carried out with round-grain, dry sand having a grain size between 0.160 mm and 0.315 mm, in a volume of 25 ml ± 0.15 ml, spread by a flat circular disc of 65 mm diameter, one side covered with a rubber sheet of 1.5 mm to 2.5 mm thickness and the other provided with a handle; the mean sand depth is calculated from the diameter D of the sand-covered area.
The surface on which the sandy beach test is to be carried out shall be dry and at first be brushed with a soft brush to remove any dirt or loose gravel.

In the sandy beach test, the sand firmly filled into a receptacle is poured in a single heap on the surface and spread by repeated circular movements of the rubber-faced disc to form the largest possible round area covered with sand.

In the sandy beach test, two diameters at right angles to one another of the sand beach are measured, the mean value rounded off to the nearest 5 mm, and the sand depth HS calculated according to the formula in paragraph 4.2.2.

Six sandy beach tests are carried out on the supporting surface, distributed as evenly as possible, and the overall mean of the results is given as the mean sand depth HS of the road surface where the advance warning triangle is placed.

For the wind stability test, the advance warning triangle shall be set up in a wind tunnel on a base measuring about 1.50 m by 1.20 m with a surface of abrasive material of type P36 corresponding to FEPA specification 43-1-2006.
The base surface for the wind stability test shall have a geometric roughness HS = 0.5 mm ± 0.05 mm, determined by the sandy beach method according to paragraph 4.
To avoid a laminar boundary layer, the base for the wind stability test shall have a splitter plate and shall be set up such that the flow is completely around the plate.
In the wind stability test, the air stream shall reach a dynamic pressure of 180 Pa and shall have a flow field which is homogeneous and free of turbulence.

In the wind stability test, the flow field shall be dimensioned such that horizontally to each corner and vertically to the top of the advance warning triangle a clearance of at least 150 mm to the border line of the flow field exists.
In the wind stability test, the air stream shall be parallel to the supporting surface, in the direction which seems most unfavourable for the stability of the advance warning triangle.
In the wind stability test, the area of the advance warning triangle shall be not larger than 5 per cent of the cross-section area of the closed wind tunnel.
condition: in the case of a closed wind tunnel

text: The advance warning triangle shall be subjected for 3 minutes to the air stream.
In the wind stability test, the advance warning triangle shall neither overturn nor shift; slight shifting of the points of contact with the road surface by not more than 5 cm shall be allowed.

In the wind stability test, the retro-reflecting triangular part of the advance warning triangle shall not rotate through more than 10° round a horizontal axis or a vertical axis from its initial position, determined with a virtual plane at the initial position orthogonal to the base and to the air stream.
The approval number shall be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
The digits constituting the approval number shall face the same way as the "E".
The group of symbols indicating the class shall be diametrically opposite the approval number.
The Type Approval Authorities shall avoid using approval numbers IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA which might be confused with the class symbols IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA.
At least one rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles shall be installed on slow-moving vehicles and their trailers which by construction cannot travel faster than 30 km/h.
condition: vehicles which by construction cannot travel faster than 30 km/h, where required by Governments
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: The rear marking plate(s) for slow moving vehicles shall be type approved and meet the requirements of this Regulation.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: The apex of a rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles shall be directed upwards.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: Every part of a rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles shall lie within 5° of a transverse vertical plane at right angles to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle and shall face to the rear.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: In width: the rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles shall be on the opposite side of the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle to the direction of traffic prescribed in the country of registration.
condition: if there is only one rear marking plate
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: In height: the rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm (lower edge) and not more than 1,500 mm (upper edge).
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: In length: the rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: Geometric visibility of the rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles: horizontal angle 30° inwards and outwards; covering by indispensable constructional parts of the vehicle up to 10 per cent of the rear marking plate surface is permitted.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: Geometric visibility of the rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles: vertical angle 15° above and below the horizontal.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles

text: The rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles shall be oriented rearwards.
applies_to: rear marking plate for slow moving vehicles
